newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN AIRLINES TO BUY UP TO 18 AIRCRAFT.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN AIRLINES TO BUY UP TO 18 AIRCRAFT.

text.p: Indian Airlines is looking to buy up to eighteen, 50 seater aircraft worth some $360 million, cargo sources at the airline said.
They said bids for the Franco-Italian ATR 42-500, the Canadian Bombardier Dash-8 and the Swedish SAAB 2000 were being studied.
The Indian Airlines Board will decide the winner in September and begin negotiations for an initial purchase of six aircraft.
The planes will be operated by Indian Airlines subsidiary Alliance Air in the northeast of the country.
All airlines are supposed to fly 10 percent of their services to difficult regions like the northeast. Indian Airlines carries the main burden of such high cost services with 17 percent of flights.

To tempt private operators the Finance Ministry has suggested that, if they exceed their 10 percent, they might be allowed to fly foreign routes and get fuel nearer to the cheaper international price.

IA has decided to increase cargo, maintenance hangar and other facilities in Calcutta, in part to support northeast expansion. IA's north-eastern management in Calcutta have said they also want to operate 100-seater aircraft in the region. They said the new hangar will be big enough to accommodate one 747, or two 100-seater planes.
